newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST-New Zealand business weeklies - Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-New Zealand business weeklies - Nov 8.

text.p: THE NATIONAL BUSINESS REVIEW

The new registrar-general of land, Brendan Boyle, has turned down six applications for landbrokers' licences, making it difficult for Australian non-lawyer conveyancers to operate here. He also reaffirmed tough criteria for granting landbrokers' licences to local applicants, insisting on a law degree and work experience as prerequisites. Page 5.

The launch of Clear Communications' Clear Net is likely to spell the beginning of the end for many of the smallest Internet service providers. Like Telecom, Clear has an advantage in being able to promote the service to its existing client base and include Internet charges on its customer accounts. Page 7.

The Alliance has asked the auditor-general to investigate the setting up of a $563,000 fund for parties involved in the coalition talks. The cabinet agreed to provide the money for employing professional policy advisers apparently after prompting from NZ First. "New expenditure cannot be authorised

by a caretaker government acting alone," Alliance leader Jim Anderton said. A senior parliamentary source agreed the case raised important issues. "It does smack a little of a political party bringing in a policy that gives it some short-term advantage."

The lobby representing the country's major brewers, DB Group and Lion Nathan, has stepped up its campaign against health warnings on bottles and cans. The Beer Wine and Spirits Council described health-warning labels as "ineffective...for adressing complex social and personal problems leading to alcohol abuse."

Telecom has just introduced Mobile Extension, which allows business users to dial fixed-line and mobile extension numbers inside their firm from a cellphone. He will not say who is going to get it, or for what. NZ First has long declined to disclose its private sector economic advisers, with Peters insisting they were of "significant credibility". Clear enters the stormy New Zealand Internet service provider (ISP) market on Friday with the launch of Clear Net. While a late entrant into a market that already has over 30 ISPs, Clear is convinced that jumping on the service and quality bandwagon will win it Internet market share. And with its main rival Telecom, whose Xtra product has around 50 percent of the
market, the battle will not be an unfamiliar one. Page 5.

Ostrich farming in South Africa is not the gold-spinner New Zealand investors have been led to believe. Ostrich breeders often cite the South African industry as a good example of the high returns that cam be made. But Whangarei lawyer Cor Eckhart, an expatriate South African, says ostrich farming in that country has never been lucrative. South African farmers view the birds as temperamental and disease-prone. Page 5.

Cut-price and charter airlines may be the greatest beneficiaries in the trans-Tasman single aviation market, says an Australian airline analyst. Former Qantas executive, now airline analyst with the Queensland Tourism Board, Ray Jeppersen predicts small airlines will increasingly link regional centres. Page 7.
